page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right. Signature mark "v" at the foot left, catchword-like word "divisa" is part of the sentence and stays in the text.

main_text.p: hospitia sua quemadmodum advenientibus humana erant, ipsis quoque tuta essent. Hactenus de civili ordine, & vetustis Massiliæ institutis. Dicenda nunc reliqua. Vltimis libertatis Romanæ temporibus & sub primis Cæsaribus a-moto omni belli metu, & armorum usu exolescente, civitas tota in studia philosophiæ & eloquentiæ versa, & ex iis clarum nomen adepta est, ut Romani, qui discendi cupidi erant, non secus Massiliam, quàm Athenas aut Rhodum, aut Alexandriam proficiscerentur, ibique studiis istis operam darent, habereturque Massilia velut officina quædam literaria. Cujus exemplo motæ Galliarum civitates aliæ iisdem disciplinis animos adjicere, & publicis privatisque stipendiis conductos dicendi magistros alere coeperunt. Atque hoc loco facere non possum, quin summorum virorum veterum judicia de civitate hac adscribam. Inter eos Cicero in oratione pro L. Valerio Flacco sic ait:

p.i: Neque vero te Massilia praetereo, qua L. Flaccum militem Quaestoremque cognosti: cujus ego civitatis disciplinam atque gravitatem non solum Gracia, sed haud scio, an cunctis gentibus anteponendam jure dicam: quam iam procul a Gracorum omnium regionibus, disciplinis, linguaque divisa.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "praetereo" (the scan is faint at the end of the word; read as praetereo, transcribed as praetereo [?] in the sense intended); "qua" for quae and "Gracia" for Graeciae are copied as the scan shows them, not corrected. Catchword "divisa" is the last word of the sentence and is kept in the text. Show-through of the reverse page (e.g. "lingu" at the lower right, marks at the left edge) is not transcribed. The left margin carries only stains and show-through, no printed notes.
